observations.behavior: Adds a guard to prevent loading available requests when no request is currently selected.
observations.posthog_connection: Preserves the picker's selection state and avoids unnecessary API calls while retaining access to requests outside the default page.

observations.behavior: Updates the clearing behavior of the request picker input; it now retains the selected ID instead of clearing it immediately on clear. This preserves selections across pagination or other transient clears.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows users to retain their chosen feature request for linking even after typing in the picker without selecting from its current results, supporting broader account association without losing context.

observations.behavior: Changes test assertions to include an explicit sequence where setting a non-empty search followed by clearing the input still leaves the requestId intact before linking.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides regression protection against unintended loss of user-selected associations during interaction with the account-level feature request picker.

observations.limitations: Only frontend TypeScript changes are supplied; backend compatibility and complete end-to-end behavior cannot be independently verified. No tier-3 systemic benefit demonstrated.

review.limitations: Only frontend TypeScript changes are supplied; backend compatibility and complete end-to-end behavior cannot be independently verified. No tier-3 systemic benefit demonstrated.
review.reason: The change adds bounded preservation of account-feature-request associations when clearing the picker input, supported by implementation and tests. It is not broad enough for tier 3 but represents a substantive reliability improvement over previous clearing behavior.
review.posthog_relevance: Relevant to Account tab workflows: retaining selectable requests while searching improves usability and prevents accidental disassociation of accounts from requested features.
review.uncertainty: Assessment relies solely on provided hunks; no access to full component or shared state dependencies.
